rounds.text: Yogi Infra Projects Ltd is heavily discounted by the market, trading at an exceptionally low price-to-book ratio of 0.27x against a book value of ₹ 21.0 [E1], while sector benchmarks show a higher P/B of 0.3x to 1.25x [E6]. Operational generation demonstrates fundamental strength through a substantial operating cash flow of Rs 31.18 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs 4.01 Cr in March 2026 [E29, E30]. Profitability is showing strong acceleration with a compounded profit growth of 37% over the trailing twelve months alongside an expanding operating margin that reached 6% in the TTM compared to just 1% three years earlier [E15, E24]. Furthermore, capital expenditure is actively scaling up with Capital Work in Progress surging by 78.4% to reach Rs 61.51 Cr in March 2026, while total borrowings simultaneously decreased to Rs 56.44 Cr [E33, E34], and insider confidence is reinforced by promoters increasing their stake to 44.60% [E35]. Conceded: [E13], [E19], [E31], [E45], [E46].

Yogi Infra Projects Ltd presents significant fundamental weaknesses that undermine its low price-to-book multiple. Compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months has collapsed by 77% [E13], reflecting severe top-line deterioration that aligns with a rules-based screen score of 40 out of 100 yielding a medium-confidence SELL recommendation [E46]. Furthermore, profitability metrics are deeply depressed, evidenced by a trailing return on equity of -0.44% [E8] and a 10-year median return on equity of 0% [E20], alongside explicitly flagged concerns regarding a low interest coverage ratio [E42]. Operational efficiency is rapidly degrading as debtor days have ballooned from 49.9 to 105 days [E44] and working capital days have worsened drastically from -38.0 days to 254 days [E45]. Leverage also introduces substantial balance sheet risk, with a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.60x indicating that debt exceeds net worth [E31], paired with a thin current ratio buffer of 1.47x [E32]. Quarterly results compound these worries, showing an operating margin of -712% in June 2026 [E25] and declining year-over-year net profit [E47]. Conceded: [E1] and [E30], the company trades at 0.27 times its book value and generated positive free cash flow of Rs 4.01 Cr in March 2026.

The bear’s focus on top-line deterioration ignores the company’s significant investment in future capacity, as Capital Work in Progress (CWIP) has surged by 78.4% to Rs 61.51 Cr, signaling a deliberate growth-oriented build-up phase rather than mere decline [E34]. While the bear highlights short-term sales volatility [E13], it overlooks that the company successfully generated Rs 31.18 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 4.01 Cr in free cash flow as of March 2026, proving the business can generate liquidity despite accounting losses [E29, E30]. Conceded: [E31, E44, E45], the debt-to-equity ratio is 1.60x, and working capital and debtor days have indeed increased. However, the bear fails to acknowledge that management is actively deleveraging, having reduced total borrowings from Rs 57.96 Cr to Rs 56.44 Cr over the last year [E33]. Furthermore, the bear’s reliance on the 40/100 screen score [E46] ignores the positive momentum in profitability, where compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months reached 37% [E15] and operating margins improved by 6 percentage points over the last three years [E24]. Finally, the market’s extreme undervaluation at 0.27x book value [E1] suggests that the current price already accounts for the bear's cited risks, while the increase in promoter holdings to 44.60% demonstrates internal confidence in the company's long-term trajectory [E35].

Conceded: [E34, E29, E30, E33]. While the bull points to positive operating and free cash flows alongside slight debt reduction and rising CWIP, these metrics mask severe structural decay. The massive surge in Capital Work in Progress to Rs 61.51 Cr represents an immense capital lockup that, combined with soaring debtor days leaping from 49.9 to 105 days and working capital days blowing out to 254 days, signals an inability to efficiently monetize operations [E34, E44, E45]. Furthermore, the bull's focus on a 37% TTM profit growth figure [E15] completely ignores the overriding collapse in top-line demand, evidenced by a catastrophic -77% compounded sales growth over the same trailing period and a negative rules-based screen score of 40 out of 100 [E13, E46]. The low valuation multiple of 0.27x book value [E1] is not an arbitrary discount to exploit, but a rational reflection of chronic wealth destruction manifested in a 10-year median ROE of 0% and a low interest coverage ratio [E20, E42]. Finally, the minor uptick in promoter holdings [E35] provides little comfort against a backdrop of negative returns on equity, negative returns on assets, and a plummeting share price down 47% over the past year [E7, E8, E19].
